label: copy phase of length-3 sequences (strongest on the final output step)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never on original tokens or <DEL>. About 73% of activation mass comes from L=3 sequences, where the rate is 48x baseline. It is strongest at t=5 (recall_idx=2, the last output, where the input is the fed-back second token); t=4 is weaker. Inside L=3 the input token changes magnitude (u, g, v, j, i are highest, digits lower), but no token set is clean enough to use. Smaller and scattered contributions: L=9 at its last output (recall_idx=8, ~6% of mass), L=4 at recall_idx 1-3 (~7%), and isolated mid-copy steps in L=6-9. Never fires when in_first=1. Precision is only partial: about 40% of L=3 copy steps are inactive.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=16: g, 2, i, 1; t=11: g, i, 2, j; t=6: g, u, 2, p) and the previous input (most: 1, k, 2, j, z, b; least: o, r, i, x); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=5, L=3 & t=4.
